messages.author: e1b933a0d5bbe14f
messages.subject: Dealing with EOF warnings in SCAN
parts:
I have a few thousand text files I need to read in, but every now and then I'll get an EOF message with scan (I want quote set to ["] ; setting it to ['] produces no warnings, but of course gives me hundreds of thousands of unslightly backslahes and quotation marks). What I want to do is get the file names of the problem files so I can deal with them. There are about 160 such files, so I don't want to manually break with options(warn=2) and record them myself. The following code doesn't work, but it shows what I'm trying to do.

file.names<-dir('C:/The_files',full.names=T,recursive=T)
assign('last.warning',NULL,envir=baseenv()) #to reset the warnings from the last run
problems<-0
problem.files<-c()
for(file in 1:length(file.names)){
current<-scan(file.names[file],what='char',sep='\n',quote='"',quiet=T)
if(length(warnings())>problems){
    problem.files<-c(problem.files,file)
    problems<-problems+1
} #close IF
} #next file

The logic is that when there's a warning, length(warning()) will increment and I can record the file number in problem.files. But if I copy and paste the code into the console, warnings() strangely doesn't seem to actually increment until after the code has finished running (last.warning neither). Afterwards, length(warnings()) will tell me the number of problems, but not while the code is running. Changing options(warn=x) doesn't affect this.

I don't care if I get this working with a variant of this code; any other approach to get R to record the file variable will make me just as happy. (Alternatively, is there a way to scan with quote=" ' " and then convert the quote mark to "?)


--
Kevin Parent, Ph.D
Korea Maritime University

messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Dealing with EOF warnings in SCAN
parts:
Again, sorry to have asked the same question twice, months apart. I got sidetracked on another project at the time, and when I returned to it, I had completely forgotten the earlier conversation. I got it working with this (snippet):

for(file.no in 1:length(file.names)){
tryCatch(current<-scan(file.names[file.no],what='char',quiet=T,quote='"',sep='\n'),warning=function(c){
c$message<-file.no
problem.files<<-c(problem.files,as.numeric(c[1]))
} #close warning function
) #close tryCatch
} #next file.no

Stefan, if you're still taking requests on what to include in the revision, a brief chapter on troubleshooting/debugging might come in handy. I found the ?tryCatch documentation pretty COIK (Clear Only If Known), and much of what I found on the web on it assumes you know similar processes in other languages.
